filo update FILE [--dry-run]

  Reads an exported retention CSV and applies the file_date and retention you
  changed. retention is a period counted from file_date (7y, 18m, 6w, 30d),
  forever, or a date (YYYY-MM-DD); file_date is a date. keep_until is worked out
  by filo: leave it alone. Dates in the past are fine: the file is then past its
  retention (see filo delete). Rows can be sorted, filtered or deleted, but not
  added. A blank retention clears a stored one; filo lists those files and asks
  first, and without a terminal leaves them alone. A row is refused, with one
  line saying why, if a value does not parse, a period has no file_date, the
  file changed since the export, or its retention was changed from a later
  export. The other rows are still applied.

  A tags CSV (from export tags) is told by its header: each tags cell replaces
  its file's tags, so an untouched cell changes nothing and an emptied one
  removes them all. Before removing any tag, filo lists those rows and asks;
  without a terminal it leaves them alone. A row is refused if a tag breaks the
  spelling rules or the file was tagged since the export.

  A duplicates CSV (from export duplicates) is refused: its decisions are not
  recorded, but carried out by filo delete FILE.

Flags
  --dry-run                check everything and write nothing
